easy.def: A big animal with a horn on its nose.
examples: We saw a rhino at the zoo.

more.def: A large, heavy animal with thick skin and one or two horns on its nose, short for rhinoceros.
examples: A rhino charged across the grassy plain.
The rhino has thick skin and a big horn on its nose.
Rhinos are in danger because people hunt them for their horns.

easy.def: A big animal with a horn on its nose.

more.def: A large animal with thick skin and one or two horns on its nose.
examples: A rhinoceros charged across the plain.
The rhinoceros has thick, gray skin.

easy.def: A stem that grows sideways under the ground.

more.def: A thick underground stem that grows sideways and sends up new shoots.
examples: A rhizome sends up new shoots.
The iris spreads by its rhizome.

easy.def: A bush with big, bright flowers.
examples: A rhododendron grows by the gate.

more.def: A large bush with thick, shiny leaves and clusters of bright flowers.
examples: Pink rhododendrons bloomed along the garden path.
The rhododendron blooms in late spring.
A rhododendron bush grew by the gate.

easy.def: A plant with red stalks that people eat cooked.

more.def: A plant with thick red stalks that are cooked with sugar and used in pies.
examples: Grandma baked a pie with rhubarb.
Rhubarb is sour, so people add sugar to it.
The rhubarb leaves are not safe to eat.

easy.def: Words that end with the same sound.

more.def: Words that have the same sound at the end, or a short poem that uses them.
examples: The nursery rhyme was easy to remember.
She wrote a rhyme about her dog.

easy.def: To end with the same sound.

more.def: To have the same sound at the end, as two words do.
examples: Poets often choose words that rhyme at the ends of their lines.
The last words in each line of the poem rhyme.
The drum has a good rhythm.

more.def: A regular pattern of beats or sounds that repeats.
examples: We clapped along to the rhythm of the song.
The dancers moved to the rhythm of the drums.
The rhythm of the rain on the roof was calming.
We clapped to the rhythmic beat.

more.def: Having a regular, repeating beat or pattern.
examples: We clapped along to the rhythmic drumming.
The rhythmic sound of the train put me to sleep.
The poem has a rhythmic pattern.

more.def: In a way that has a regular beat or pattern.
examples: The dancers swayed rhythmically to the music.
The waves lapped rhythmically against the shore.
